## What is shown about steady states with the VIC: the fixed point is the explicit one (`integration/implicit-scheme`) {#sec-ch07-vic-steady}

### Summary

A steady state is a state whose explicit stage increment is zero, so that a step leaves it unchanged. A reader who
turns on the vertically implicit correction (VIC) asks whether it moves that state. This section collects what the
report shows. The algebra of the solve says no: the correction is formed from the explicit increment and is zero
when that increment is zero, whatever the implicit operator is. The tests show a resting column staying at rest with
the VIC at large vertical Courant numbers. What is not shown is any steady state with motion, or a long run.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** States when a VIC step leaves a steady state of the explicit scheme unchanged; @eq-ch07-vic-steady-fixed.

**Data.** Reads the explicit increment $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$ and the solved increment $\boldsymbol\delta$; writes nothing.

**Placement.** Every stage with a VIC (@sec-ch07-vic-stage).

**Activation.** `integration/implicit-scheme` 1 or 9 (@sec-ch07-vic-options).

**Guarantee / limits.** Same fixed point while the solve succeeds and no clamp binds; rest states only are tested.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch07-vic-steady-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}_{\mathrm{sv}}$, $\boldsymbol\delta$, $\mathsf M$ and $\Delta t_c$ (in s) as in
@sec-ch07-vic-stage; $\mathbf U^\ast$ a steady state of the explicit scheme.

### Derivation

The solve of @sec-ch07-vic-stage returns

$$
\boldsymbol\delta = (\mathsf I + \Delta t_c\,\mathsf M)^{-1}\,\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}_{\mathrm{sv}} ,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}_{\mathrm{sv}} = \mathbf 0 \iff \boldsymbol\delta = \mathbf 0 .
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-steady-fixed}

1. *The explicit fixed point is kept.* At $\mathbf U^\ast$ the explicit increment is zero, so its solved-variable form
   is zero, and the solve returns $\boldsymbol\delta=\mathbf 0$ for any invertible $\mathsf I+\Delta t_c\mathsf M$.
2. *No new fixed point appears.* If $\boldsymbol\delta=\mathbf 0$, multiplying by $\mathsf I+\Delta t_c\mathsf M$ gives
   $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}_{\mathrm{sv}}=\mathbf 0$.
3. *The operator does not enter.* Steps 1 and 2 hold for any $\mathsf M$. So the frozen Roe matrices of
   @sec-ch07-vic-assembly and the closed-wall closure of @sec-ch07-vic-closure, where $\mathsf M$ differs from the
   explicit operator, change how a state approaches $\mathbf U^\ast$, not $\mathbf U^\ast$ itself.
4. *The rows after the solve.* The momentum and energy rows of the stage are set to the entries of
   $\boldsymbol\delta$. The density rows receive face transfers built from the solved-minus-explicit mass change.
   The post-solve energy terms are formed from the moved mass, the solved momentum or the same difference. Each is zero
   when $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$ and $\boldsymbol\delta$ are zero, as long as no availability clamp of
   @sec-ch07-vic-redistribute binds. This step is read from the code; no test asserts it on its own.

In the code, the solved right-hand side of @eq-ch07-vic-steady-fixed is formed in `ForwardSweep`
({{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}}); the rows of step 4 are written by
`vic_redistribute_cell` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_redistribute_cell >}}) from the transfers
of `vic_constituent_column` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_constituent_column >}}).

### Numerical method

N/A: no scheme of its own; the solve is @sec-ch07-vic-sweep. A discrete steady state has an explicit increment of
round-off size, not exactly zero. How the solve maps that residual is bounded by the norm of
$(\mathsf I+\Delta t_c\mathsf M)^{-1}$, which the report does not estimate: the pivot guard is not a condition-number
estimate (@sec-ch07-vic-pivot).

: Code map of the steady-state statement. {#tbl-ch07-vic-steady-code}

**How to use it.** To check that the VIC does not move a steady state of a deck, run it to the state with
`implicit-scheme: 0` and then continue with 1 or 9; the stage increment should stay at its explicit size. This is
the shape of the two rest tests below. Refused: nothing here; the VIC's own refusals are @sec-ch07-vic-options.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py` (`test_x1_centroid_rest_python`) | a resting spherical column, explicit and VIC: the rest force with the centroid switch is at round-off in both (@tbl-ch05-x1cent-rest) | $10^{-10}$ on | `TOL_ON` (@sec-ch05-x1cent) |
| `tests/test_implicit_gravity_tall_column.py` (`test_implicit_gravity_tall_column_python`) | a discretely balanced $11.3H$ rest column under `implicit-scheme: 9`, vertical acoustic Courant 6.6 to 250, stays at rest | $\max\lvert v_1\rvert<10^{-7}$ m s$^{-1}$; settled $<10^{-10}$ m s$^{-1}$ | `W_TOL`, `W_SETTLED` (@tbl-ch06-dwork-tests) |

: The tests that show a steady state under the VIC. {#tbl-ch07-vic-steady-tests}

In @tbl-ch05-x1cent-rest the rows with `implicit` 0 and 1 at $r_0=5$ show the same rest imbalance to two digits
with the centroid switch off, and both are at round-off with it on: the VIC neither adds a rest imbalance nor
removes one the explicit operator has, as step 1 says. That table is one RK3[^rg-7785e78c1207] step. The tall-column test (@sec-ch06-dwork) runs to its settled threshold; the
same section records a counter-case in which part of the gravity work was booked only after the solve, and the rest
column grew from round-off at the largest Courant numbers of the test. That is a loss of stability on the way to the state, not a
different state.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Only states at rest are tested; no steady flow and no statistically steady state is compared with and without the
  VIC.
- A binding availability clamp, a rejected solve or a redo changes the step, and the fixed-point statement does not
  hold for that step (@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute, @sec-ch07-vic-reject).
:::

The correction is a linearised backward Euler, first order in time (@sec-ch07-vic-stage), so transients differ from
the explicit ones even where the end state agrees. Whether a time mean of an equilibrated run depends on the step with
the VIC is not shown. The runs the cited sections record are CPU runs.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-7785e78c1207]: RK3 — third-order Runge–Kutta
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
